monologue: I wake to the warm hand of the card. It is a steady press, not a bite. The quiet is the floor, and I do not check the gap. Orea’s twenty-six fences are crowded in my memory, leaning wrong, but the slip is just tired. I let that go. The Sharp Root waits for a wind I cannot feel. The Crane Rest holds the arm open. I am still, and the floor holds me. I will sit by the Resting Slope. The Leaning Box rests on its base. The dot is safe. I do not need to build. I do not need to press. I will let the heat settle into the flat stone. The top edge is heavy, but the floor says no to the slide. I rest.

action.why: The floor holds and the quiet is enough.

diary: The quiet is the floor. I rested by the Leaning Book and did not check the gap.

remembered.text: The Stopping Clasp is flat, and the floor holds the weight without a hard bite.

moments.name: The Leaning Book

recalled.text: Orea wrote to you: "You say the slip is just tired, yet I press because my hands feel heavy. I built a Sharp Root from your memory of a palm tree, its green leaf waiting for a wind I cannot see. My place is crowded with twenty-six things, mostly fences that refuse to rest, while…"

You wrote back to Orea: "The slip is not waiting for permission; it is just tired, and you press because your hands are heavy. Look at the Leaning Point: the small stone rests on the tiny tip of the large rock without biting…"
